🇲🇽⚖️ <u>MEXICO DEFEATS VULCAN MATERIALS AT ICSID: 99% OF THE $1.5BN CLAIM REJECTED</u>

A World Bank tribunal dismissed nearly all of Vulcan Materials' $1,529 million claim against Mexico over the Calica limestone quarry in Quintana Roo — shut down for documented ecological damage and later declared a protected natural area. The ICSID panel upheld only one measure tied to a January 2018 closure of a single Calica site, and the compensation recognized represents less than 1% of what the Alabama company demanded, the Economy Ministry said. Mexico is reviewing the ruling for further legal action.

🚨🇲🇽 <u>ARMY AND NATIONAL GUARD DISMANTLE MEGA METH LAB IN MICHOACÁN</u>

Federal forces dismantled a clandestine synthetic drug laboratory hidden in dense vegetation in Carácuaro, Michoacán, seizing 10,580 liters of chemical precursors, 3,225 kilograms of solid inputs, eight organic synthesis reactors and eight industrial condensers. The economic blow to organized crime is estimated at 3,224 million pesos — one of the largest financial hits recorded this year. The Federal Prosecutor's Office opened an investigation and patrols are being reinforced across the region to locate additional camps.

🇲🇽📱 <u>MEXICO OPENS PUBLIC DEBATE ON REGULATING SOCIAL MEDIA FOR MINORS</u>

The federal government is launching an evidence-based national discussion on children's access to social media, SEP chief Mario Delgado announced, with neurodevelopment and addiction specialists presenting their research at the mañanera. One data point landed hard: twenty years ago a person could focus on a screen for about 2.5 minutes before getting distracted; today that time is down to roughly 47 seconds, said Lucía Magis Weinberg of the University of Washington's Digital Youth Center. Sheinbaum said the government is preparing materials for parents on the risks of excessive use. "The important thing is we're taking on this challenge together," Delgado said.

🇲🇽🐄 <u>US REOPENS BORDER TO MEXICAN CATTLE — GRADUALLY, STARTING WITH SONORA</u>

After more than a year of joint technical work against the screwworm, the United States will reopen its border to Mexican cattle in the second or third week of August, President Sheinbaum announced. The USDA opens the Douglas, Arizona port of entry on August 24, then reviews Santa Teresa and Columbus in New Mexico. The key: Mexico's sterile fly plant in Metapa, Chiapas and artisanal traps that brought the pest under control. Even US Agriculture Secretary Brooke Rollins admitted the closure was a "difficult measure." Technical work, not threats, is what reopened the border.

🚨🇲🇽 <u>"MEXICO MUST NOT DEFINE YOUR CAMPAIGN": SHEINBAUM ANSWERS STEPHEN MILLER</u>

After White House deputy chief of staff Stephen Miller claimed drug cartels "control" territory in Mexico, President Sheinbaum answered without entering his game: "Mexico must not be the defining element of their campaign — it must be the United States itself." Her message to Washington: look in the mirror at your own drug consumption, distribution and money laundering. "In Mexico the people govern, no one else. We combat and work every day for security and peace in our country, and there are results," she said, pointing to coordination where each side operates in its own territory.
banner: SHEINBAUM TO MILLER: FIX YOUR HOUSE

🚨🇲🇽 <u>SPACEX DEBRIS ON THE BORDER: MEXICO SETS THE RULES</u>

President Sheinbaum says Mexico will not sue SpaceX — for now — over rocket debris from its Texas launch pad falling into Mexican territory. The choice was coordination with teeth: a launch-notification protocol enforced by a federal team from SRE to the Navy, and an explicit warning to Musk's company and the US government. "They can't have launch residues falling on national territory. So far, more or less, it has worked. If a lawsuit becomes necessary, we'll evaluate it," she said. Digital chief José Merino confirmed the latest Starship launch left zero debris in Mexican territory or waters. The pad on the Tamaulipas border has operated since 2014. Mexico put it on notice.
